text:
Samira Khan: Hi everyone! Samira joining Cloud Infra on Mon. Quick Notion Qs — I can view the 'Cloud Infra Onboarding' but its read-only. I want to duplicate the "First-week checklist" and share an editable copy with my manager. Who owns the canonical and what's the fastest way to get page-level edit access? Also worried about breaking automations if we move copies.

devex: Welcome Samira! Canonical infra onboarding lives at Redwood > Eng > Cloud Infra > Onboarding. Owners are listed in the page properties. Fastest: DM @devex the full Notion page URL + your SSO email and we can add page-level Editor for a set duration (default 14d). We prefer page-level to workspace-level edits.

docs-bot: When requesting access include: 1) full page URL, 2) SSO email, 3) requested duration, 4) short reason. Example request block below. Also duplicate preserves DB properties, but external hooks reference page IDs so moving a copy can break automations.

Samira Khan: Thanks — can you drop the example request here? Also if I duplicate to "My workspace" then move it to Team space later will that break search/links?

devex: Sure — copy/paste this and edit:
```
@devex please add Editor on <NOTION_URL> for Samira Khan (samira@redwood.com)
Duration: 14 days
Reason: complete ramp checklist + share with manager
```
Moving a duplicate into Team space changes the page ID context for integrations. If the onboarding has automations (e.g., Slack notify, Jira create) those usually point at the canonical page. Two safe options: (A) get Editor on the canonical and edit in-place under a "DRAFT - <date>" heading, or (B) duplicate to Team space and add a `SourcePage` property with the canonical URL and `Status=Draft` so automations ignore it.

Ethan Cole: Hi Samira — as a manager tip: if you duplicate, add a top-level note: "DUPLICATE - For Manager Review" and a page property `IsCanonical=false`. Our automation ignores pages where `IsCanonical=false` or `Status=Draft`.

Samira Khan: Good to know. One more: the checklist references internal infra runbook links that the cohort shouldn't see. Is it OK to redact them in the duplicate?

Benji (eng): Redact in the duplicate only. If it's PII or sensitive links, replace with placeholders like `[internal-runbook-placeholder]`. If you need help identifying what to redact, tag me and I'll review quickly.

docs-bot: Quick note on DB templates: if the checklist is a database, duplicates carry column schemas. But saved views/filters are also copied; check the default view to ensure nothing is hidden (e.g., remove filters that set `Status=Archived`). Also update the default sort if you want Week 1 first.

Samira Khan: Perfect. I'll DM @devex the URL and ask for 14 days editor access for samira@redwood.com. If they prefer I can just edit in the canonical under a DRAFT heading to avoid copy headaches.

devex: That works. If you DM us the URL we'll fast-track it. If you plan to share with the cohort, include their emails in the request and we can add multiple editors. Also follow the naming conv: `Onboard - <FirstLast> - <Team> - <MonYYYY>` for personal/onboard pages.

People Ops (Rae): One more coordination point: if the checklist contains HR tasks, please cc People Ops so we don't expose forms with employee data. We can mark those sections as `HR-only` in the canonical template so duplicates show placeholders.

Samira Khan: Thanks all. Sending the DM now. Last tiny Q: where are the canonical templates maintained so I can file a doc fix if something is outdated?

Benji (eng): Canonical templates: Redwood > Eng > Templates. If you find an issue, add a comment on the page and tag the owner (property: Owner) or file a ticket in the docs backlog board with link. Small edits you can request via @devex.

Samira Khan: Awesome, appreciate the help! :wave:
